title: AI Fashion Lookbook Photos and Outfit Ads | AIVideosUGC
description: Turn one outfit photo into photos of the full outfit worn together. Use them on a collection page or a launch ad, and check each piece you can ship.
h1: AI Lookbook Photos for One Complete Outfit
lead: Upload one full outfit for a lookbook, photos of that outfit worn together. An AI actor, a generated person, can wear it. When you turn the same photo into a video, you can add a spoken voice. Credits, what each job spends, are shown before you start.
steps_h2: Make Outfit Photos for the Collection in 3 Steps
steps_lead: Upload the full outfit, name one location and one light, then download the photo for the collection page.

steps.d: Lay the full outfit in one bright photo, with each piece apart. Include the top, bottom, outer piece, and shoes if they belong.
Name one place and one kind of light. Use that same choice on every outfit so the set feels connected.
Check each piece against what you can ship. Add the price and links outside the image, and post only matching photos.

faq.q: What should the source photo include?
faq.a: Show every piece in the outfit, including the top, bottom, outer piece, and the shoes or main extra, in one photo. If a piece is missing from your photo, leave it out of the result.

faq.q: How do I keep a collection looking connected?
faq.a: Reuse one place, one light, and one framing across outfits, and keep each piece easy to tell apart. A digital twin, the same generated person, can repeat so the set feels like one shoot. Start with the main outfit.

faq.q: Can I show more than one outfit in a single image?
faq.a: Use one full outfit per image so the outline stays clear. Make a separate image for the next outfit.

faq.q: Do I need a photographer or models?
faq.a: No. Each photo is made from an outfit photo you already have. The person is an AI actor you pick from the actor list, not someone you booked and not a customer.

faq.q: How is this different from hiring a creator?
faq.a: A creator needs samples, a fee, and time on the calendar. Here you upload one photo or paste a product page link, pick a scene, and pay the credits, what that job spends.

faq.q: What does a lookbook photo cost?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits. Credits are what the job spends. The cost is shown before you start, and a failed job returns those credits. There is no free plan. The download has no watermark, nothing stamped on the file, and you can use it in your own ads, pages, and posts.

faq.q: Can the same scene cover menswear and womenswear?
faq.a: Yes. Menswear and womenswear can share one framing and one light when each outfit has its own photo. Check the fit and the lengths against the clothes you sell.

faq.q: Can I use the frames in a launch?
faq.a: Yes. They fit a collection page, a carousel (you swipe through several), or a launch email after you add prices yourself. A launch that also needs a video is covered by [product launch video and photos](page:occ-product-launch).

faq.q: Can the look include a voiceover and captions?
faq.a: The outfit photo is a still picture. When you make a video from the same outfit photo, add a spoken voice, words on screen, and a music track. Then post that video to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram).

faq.q: Can I start from a product link or another language?
faq.a: Yes. Paste a product page link and ask for a short script, the words to say. You can speak the line in another language. The API lets your product list start the next outfit. You see what the job spends before each job.

steps.prompt: An adult wears the ivory tailored suit and faces the camera. The jacket, trousers, shoes, and bag stay visible. Bright daylight keeps the full outfit easy to see.
